details: Open-source models have scaled test-time compute but stalled near the 1T-parameter class, risking a widening gap to proprietary frontier systems; the paper pursues both scaling axes at once.
Scaling a pre-trained foundation to ~3T parameters while also scaling RL, reasoning effort, and long-horizon agentic interaction at 1M-token context.
Kimi K3: a natively multimodal 2.8T-parameter MoE model (104B activated, 1M-token context) released with open weights.

Architecture scales information flow along three axes: sequence (3:1 hybrid of Kimi Delta Attention with lower-bounded channel-wise decay and NoPE Gated MLA), depth (Attention Residuals, where each layer softmax-attends over preceding block outputs via a learned pseudo-query), and width (Stable LatentMoE: 16-of-896 routed experts in a compact latent space, stabilized by RMSNorm, bounded SiTU-GLU activation, and Quantile-Balancing router bias).
Post-training trains one RL expert per (domain x reasoning-effort) cell and consolidates the nine experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
93 layers, hidden dim 7168, 96 attention heads, 69 KDA + 24 Gated MLA layers, latent MoE dim 3584 (0.5x), MoE hidden 3072/expert, 2 shared experts, 160K vocab, 1 MTP layer.
KDA log-decay parameterized as g = g_min * sigmoid(e^A z) with g_min = -5; full-rank input-dependent output gates in both KDA and MLA; MLA attention output kept in FP32 during training.
Block Attention Residuals: layers partitioned into 8 blocks of 12 (9 sources counting the embedding), reducing memory/communication from O(Ld) to O(Nd).
SiTU-GLU soft caps beta1 = 4 (gate), beta2 = 25 (up branch); Quantile Balancing estimated from all-reduced per-expert margin histograms.
Native vision: MoonViT-V2, 27 layers, ~0.4B params, patch 14, RMSNorm and bias-free, trained from scratch with next-token prediction, 2x2 pixel-shuffle, inputs up to 3584x3584.
Corpus of web text, code, math, knowledge (with K2-style rephrasing) plus a vision corpus including OCR, video, and programmatic code-render pairs (SVG, 3D, webpages, games, CAD).
Per-Head Muon optimizer (Newton-Schulz applied per attention head) with K2 weight clipping, cosine LR with 1% warmup, weight decay 0.1.

Four-stage context curriculum: 8K -> 64K during pre-training, 256K -> 1M during cooldown; NoPE so no RoPE rescaling/YaRN; long-context data cleaned, upsampled, and synthesized by permuting/concatenating multimodal sub-tasks.
Dedicated scaling-law study retuning batch size, LR, tokens-per-parameter, and model shape, evaluated on held-out OOD validation data.

SFT cold start from trajectories synthesized by prior Kimi domain experts, serialized in an XTML chat template; MXFP4 expert weights / MXFP8 activations quantization-aware training from SFT onward, with rollout and training sharing the same quantization.

RL over three domains (general tasks, general agents, coding agents) x three effort levels {low, high, max} = 9 experts; per-problem token-budget control with reward -1 on budget violation, annealed budget multiplier tau; agentic generative reward model with mandatory rubric protocol and verbosity capping.
Partial rollout: generation pauses once a fraction lambda of the N x K trajectories finish, with paused rollouts resumed next iteration; per-token regularization tolerates the resulting staleness.

Environments: unified configurable white-box agent harness (instantiating Kimi Code, Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes), knowledge-graph-guided task synthesis, GPU kernel optimization with correctness/roofline rewards plus hacking detection, persistent mock-app assistant tasks (Gmail/Notion/Slack-like, up to thousands of tool calls), Autonomous Execution Tasks with public/hidden verifiers, and web development tasks.

FlashKDA CUTLASS chunkwise kernel overlapping intra-chunk compute with cross-chunk state propagation; intra-device SM-level context-parallel planner for long prefill; KDA Context Parallelism composing per-segment cumulative transitions with zero-initialized local states.

MoonEP for perfectly balanced expert-parallel 2.8T MoE training with static shapes and zero-copy communication; resumable microVM sandboxes and external KV-cache retention for million-token agentic RL.

Speculative decoding: pre-trained MTP layer fine-tuned into an EAGLE-3 draft fusing features from the 1st, 4th, and final AttnRes blocks (fusion matrix initialized to [0 0 I]), unrolled 7 steps, trained with the likelihood-based LK acceptance-rate loss.

Benchmarks span coding (DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 2.1, FrontierSWE, SWE-Marathon, ProgramBench, internal Kimi Code Bench 2.0), agentic/general (GDPval-AA v2 Elo, BrowseComp, AutomationBench, JobBench), and vision with tools (CharXiv RQ, ZeroBench pass@5), all at maximum thinking effort.
Baselines: Claude Fable 5, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.5, GLM-5.2.

Ablations reported: SigLIP-initialized MoonViT-3D vs from-scratch MoonViT-V2 gradient norms; cosine vs WSD LR schedules with per-schedule hyperparameter searches; RL FLOP scaling curves for score and average assistant steps.

key_findings.finding: The combined architectural, data, and training changes yield roughly a 2.5x improvement in overall scaling efficiency over Kimi K2.
key_findings.evidence: Fitted scaling-law curves for K2 and K3 on held-out OOD validation data, obtained after independently retuning batch size, learning rate, tokens-per-parameter, and model shape for the new architecture (KDA hybrid attention, AttnRes, Stable LatentMoE, Per-Head Muon).

key_findings.finding: Kimi K3 reaches frontier-level performance, leading all evaluated open and most proprietary models while still trailing Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol overall.
key_findings.evidence: Best scores in the suite on BrowseComp 91.2 (vs 90.4 GPT-5.6 Sol), ProgramBench 77.8, SWE-Marathon 42.0, AutomationBench 30.8; second on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (88.3 vs 88.8), FrontierSWE (81.2 vs 86.6), JobBench (54.3 vs 57.4), CharXiv RQ with tools (91.3 vs 93.5); GDPval-AA v2 Elo 1686 vs 1747/1736 for the two strongest proprietary models.

key_findings.finding: A vision encoder trained entirely from scratch with next-token prediction is more stable than and just as capable as a contrastively pre-trained (SigLIP) initialization at scale.
key_findings.evidence: In pre-training ablations, the SigLIP-initialized MoonViT-3D shows persistently higher gradient norms with frequent spikes while MoonViT-V2 stays stable, and MoonViT-V2 matches the SigLIP-initialized baseline across vision evaluations.

key_findings.finding: Lower-bounding KDA's log-decay with a scaled sigmoid removes the intra-chunk diagonal bottleneck by keeping all rescaling factors inside BF16 range.
key_findings.evidence: With g_min = -5 every retention factor exceeds e^-5, so cumulative log-decay over a 16-token tile lies in (-80, 0) and the reciprocal rescaling factor stays below e^80; this lets both diagonal and off-diagonal tiles use dense Tensor Core matmuls instead of explicit position-pair computation.

key_findings.finding: Quantile Balancing balances ~10^3 experts by setting each expert bias to a router-score quantile, replacing the fixed-step sign update whose step size trades adaptation speed against oscillation.
key_findings.evidence: Routing with Top-(k+1) yields per-token cutoffs, and setting the bias to the negative (1 - k/n)-quantile of the score margins provably assigns each expert exactly the target load q = mk/n; at scale the quantile is read from all-reduced per-expert histograms (a few hundred bins per expert), which is exact for the pooled global batch up to bin width.
